questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L04_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

Which choice best shows a fair counterclaim?

answer.text: A. Anyone who disagrees is wrong

feedback.text: This attacks people instead of stating an opposing view.

answer.text: B. Practice is always perfect

feedback.text: This supports the claim and is not a counterclaim.

answer.text: C. Some students may feel nervous practicing in front of a peer

feedback.text: Correct. This fairly states a realistic opposing concern.

answer.text: D. Speeches have introductions

feedback.text: This is unrelated to the opposing viewpoint.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L04_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.04

Which choice best shows a direct rebuttal?

answer.text: A. Short peer practice can reduce pressure while still giving useful feedback

feedback.text: Correct. This answers the concern about nervousness directly.

answer.text: B. That concern does not matter

feedback.text: This dismisses the counterclaim instead of answering it.

answer.text: C. Everyone should just agree

feedback.text: This pressures the audience without giving reasoning.

answer.text: D. Peer practice is a phrase

feedback.text: This defines words but does not rebut the concern.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L04_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.02

Which choice best shows respectful disagreement?

answer.text: A. That idea is bad and useless

feedback.text: This attacks the idea harshly and weakens respectful communication.

answer.text: B. You clearly did not think

feedback.text: This attacks the person, not the counterclaim.

answer.text: C. No, because no

feedback.text: This is not respectful or supported.

answer.text: D. I understand the concern, but a short first practice can make feedback less stressful

feedback.text: Correct. This respects the concern and offers a reasoned response.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L04_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

Which choice best shows evidence in a rebuttal?

answer.text: A. Peer practice is good because it is good

feedback.text: This repeats the claim without evidence.

answer.text: B. A one-minute practice round gives feedback before the final presentation

feedback.text: Correct. This evidence supports why peer practice can help.

answer.text: C. Some people do not like it

feedback.text: This restates the counterclaim instead of rebutting it.

answer.text: D. The topic is speeches

feedback.text: This is too general to support a rebuttal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L04_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.04

Which choice best shows a complete counterclaim and rebuttal pair?

answer.text: A. Peer practice is best and nobody should question it

feedback.text: This ignores counterclaims and sounds dismissive.

answer.text: B. Some students are nervous, so the claim is impossible

feedback.text: This gives only the counterclaim and no rebuttal.

answer.text: C. Some students may fear peer practice; however, starting with one short section can build confidence

feedback.text: Correct. This includes both a fair counterclaim and a supported rebuttal.

answer.text: D. Practice exists, and people talk

feedback.text: This is vague and does not include a clear counterclaim or rebuttal.
